Definition: Rekab, the name of two Arabs and of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Rechab son of Rimmon fathered the two captains who murdered Ish-bosheth, and Jehonadab son of Rechab rode with Jehu to cut off the house of Ahab. Jonadab son of Rechab commanded his sons to drink no wine and build no houses, and they kept his word for generations.
TheologicalSignificance: What I see here is that the house of Rechab is remembered because obedience outlasted kings, and a father's command kept his children when the nation fell.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
